data.title: Tinea capitis — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 7 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Tinea capitis** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. Types of hair invasion?**
- Ectothrix: arthroconidia outside the shaft, destroy cuticle (Microsporum canis, M. audouinii, T. mentagrophytes, T. verrucosum)
- Endothrix: arthroconidia inside the shaft, cuticle intact (T. tonsurans, T. violaceum, T. soudanense) — black-dot
- Favus: hyphae and air spaces in shaft (T. schoenleinii)

**Q2. Clinical types?**
- Non-inflammatory: grey patch (ectothrix, scaly patches with broken hairs), black dot (endothrix), seborrhoeic/diffuse scaling type
- Inflammatory: kerion (boggy, pustular, suppurative plaque with lymphadenopathy — can scar), agminate folliculitis
- Favus: yellow cup-shaped crusts (scutula), mousy odour, scarring alopecia

**Q3. Which fungi fluoresce under Wood's lamp?**
- Green fluorescence: Microsporum canis, M. audouinii, M. ferrugineum, M. distortum; favus (T. schoenleinii) — dull blue-green
- Non-fluorescent: T. tonsurans, T. violaceum, T. soudanense (endothrix)

**Q4. Differential diagnosis?**
- Seborrhoeic dermatitis, psoriasis, alopecia areata, trichotillomania, pityriasis amiantacea, impetigo, pyoderma/bacterial folliculitis (kerion), lupus/LPP, discoid lupus

**Q5. Investigations?**
- KOH of plucked hairs/scales (spores and hyphae), Wood's lamp, trichoscopy (comma hairs, corkscrew hairs, Morse-code hairs, zigzag hairs), culture

**Q6. Treatment?**
- Systemic therapy is always needed (topicals do not penetrate the follicle)
- Griseofulvin microsize 20–25 mg/kg/day for 6–8 weeks (drug of choice for Microsporum)
- Terbinafine weight-based (10–20 kg 62.5 mg; 20–40 kg 125 mg; >40 kg 250 mg) for 2–4 weeks (T. tonsurans; 8–12 weeks for M. canis)
- Itraconazole 5 mg/kg/day; fluconazole 6 mg/kg/day
- Adjuncts: 2% ketoconazole or 2.5% selenium sulfide shampoo for patient and family (reduce spore shedding); kerion — add short oral steroid if severe; no surgical drainage

**Q7. Why is tinea capitis rare after puberty?**
- Sebum fatty acids (fungistatic) increase at puberty

## Quick spotter facts
- Scaly patch of broken hairs in a child with green fluorescence — grey patch tinea capitis (Microsporum)

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Superficial fungal infection — tinea capitis); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.18; Wolverton 4e Table 10.5. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
